title: Refuse ambiguous derived pricing model IDs instead of publishing duplicate rows. Footnote stripping in pricingNameToModelId is many-to-one, so a pricing table carrying both a plain name and the same name with a promotion footnote derives one model ID twice. Proven with a two-row source: parse produced two data entries both claiming claude-sonnet-5, pricingForModel silently returned the first price, and publishCopilotPricing emitted two rows with the same model ID, which a downstream consumer would reject and which violates an (etag, model_id) uniqueness constraint. The two prices differ by design because a promotion row is often 0.00, so selecting either states a confident wrong price. Detect derived-ID collisions across distinct display names, refuse every colliding row by leaving its model null, preserve all of them in unmatched_models, and deduplicate that diagnostic. No live collision exists in the current pricing table, so this is a latent defect rather than an active outage.
